failures.evidence: A linked image whose link carries a character reference or a backslash escape is stored with its link as written, not as CommonMark and the browser editor read it. (1) differential.sh --base 7af60a22b33f --head 6a206afc --corpus tester/corpus/adversarial.jsonl (48 adversarial shapes) exits 1 with 'GATE head loses a whole-image link ... 1' (adversarial:dest-escaped, [![x](i.png)](https://u.com/\)x)); with tester/corpus/control.jsonl it is 2 (linked-dest-amp [![x](i.png)](https://u.com/?a=1&b=2), linked-dest-backslash-star [![x](i.png)](https://u.com/\*x)): head's tree holds link 'https://u.com/?a=1&b=2' where the engine reads 'https://u.com/?a=1&b=2'. (2) In the real browser (throwaway spec zz-tester-linked.e2e.ts T1, chromium, against the head server), the same document written by an agent draws the live editor's anchor as href="https://ci.example/q?a=1&b=2" and href="https://ci.example/a\*b", while the past-version view and the comment draw https://ci.example/q?a=1&b=2 and https://ci.example/a*b: one document, two different links. Cause: parse.go:950 takes href = current.Destination raw for a link, while parseImage decodes src with unescapeMarkdownText (parse.go:836); the linked-image branch (parse.go:959-967) stores that raw href as the image's link. Red test: TestParseDecodesALinkedImagesLinkAsTheEditorReadsIt in packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/pmdoc/parse_test.go (commit 80ac2d84fc67); 'cd packages/envoy && go test ./internal/dispatch/pmdoc/ -run TestParseDecodesALinkedImagesLinkAsTheEditorReadsIt' fails with image link = "https://u.com/?a=1&b=2", want "https://u.com/?a=1&b=2" (and the two escape cases). Text links carry the same raw href at base and head (live editor draws href="...&b=2" for [text-amp](https://ci.example/q?a=1&b=2) too); whether the fix also decodes a text link's href is a scope decision sent to the architect.
